purpose: Every owner of FASTPQ-style field/AIR/FRI/transcript/commitment code in the workspace, the production consumers that use each one, and every importer. crates/fastpq_prover/tests/shared_backend_inventory.rs fails when a listed path or symbol disappears, when an importer appears or disappears (file by file, also inside a listed tree), when a constant equal to the Goldilocks modulus is defined in an unlisted file, when a new *stark*/*fri* source file is not covered, when a chip module is added at any depth, when a sealed q77 relation type is added, or when a path recorded as having no engine starts importing one.

scan.matching: Line comments are removed. A needle matches only at identifier boundaries; a fragment (identifier characters only, at least 12 bytes) matches any identifier that contains it, also inside a string literal. A rule matches a file when any needle or fragment and every `also` token match, the file is under one of `within` (when given) and under none of `exclude`. Files under an engine's owner_paths are never its importers. A `tree` importer lists in `files` every matching file below it; the tree is one migration unit. Hidden directories and skip_directories are not entered; exclude_files holds the checker itself, whose self-test strings would otherwise match. A Goldilocks modulus definition is a `const` or `static` of type u64 or u128 whose initializer evaluates to 2^64 - 2^32 + 1 in any spelling (literals, MAX constants, casts, `from`, shifts and arithmetic, on one line or several), or whose name claims the modulus while its initializer cannot be evaluated and is not a plain rename of another constant.

canonical_owner.replacement: B.2 generalizes this engine behind fastpq_prover::air; B.3 moves every importer of a duplicate owner to it.
canonical_owner.limits: air::WorkLimits is the one work-limit value of every owner behind the interface. The committed engine takes it only inside air::q77::VerifierLimits (bounded verification) and air::q77::ProducerLimits (whole-attempt plan); the public quantity facade maps VerifyLimits, VerificationLimits and ProvingLimits to them with for_segment. B.3 moves VerifyLimits out of the superseded driver file src/proof.rs.

roles_without_an_engine.plan_role: RAM-LFE program classes (affine, bounded, refresh), verifiable opening and threshold opening
roles_without_an_engine.finding: No RAM-LFE path proves or verifies with a FASTPQ-style engine today. Core refuses proof mode: policy validation and receipt verification both return PROOF_RELATION_UNAVAILABLE and never reach a verifier; the Core file's only use of the generic verification facade is a negative-control test showing that a valid proof of another relation is still refused. iroha_crypto's RAM-LFE code has no STARK, FRI or AIR code; it uses the fastpq_isi Digest384 hash for commitments only. The three iroha_core_zk modules are test-only Halo2 capacity experiments for the unavailable relation and belong to the distinct Halo2 family. The checker fails when a listed path starts importing a proof engine.
roles_without_an_engine.planned: R.11 (client well-formedness and circuit privacy) depends on B.1; R.2, R.3 and R.8 (phone-control, affine execution, verifiable opening and identifier PRF) depend on B.2; R.12, R.7, R.9 and R.10 deliver the affine, bounded, refresh and threshold flows. Whether a relation uses the shared FASTPQ backend and its transcript follows from the construction R.0 selects, not from a switch. Each one becomes a consumer entry here when it lands.
